articles.title_original: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
articles.title_en: Bilayer graphene demonstrates gate-tunable proximity superconductivity
articles.excerpt_original: Van der Waals heterostructures offer a direct way of combining two-dimensional (2D) materials with different electronic properties, such as 2D semiconductors, metals, and superconductors, in a single device. Bilayer graphene (BLG) is particularly attractive in this context, as its electrically tunable band gap enables local control of tunnel barriers and quantum dots. Here, we realize an all-2D hybrid platform based on BLG proximitized by superconducting NbSe$_2$. Using local electrostatic gates, we define tunnel barriers and quantum dots at different distances from the lateral superconductor-semiconductor interface. The quantum dots serve as local spectroscopic probes of the proximitized BLG channel segment, forming tunable superconductor-quantum dot-normal conductor junction devices. Coulomb blockade and finite-bias spectroscopy reveal a proximity-induced superconducting gap of up to $80\,\mathrm{μeV}$ and allow to track its evolution with increasing distance from the NbSe$_2$ contact. We find that the local density of states remains suppressed over distances exceeding 1 $μ$m, consistent with superconducting proximity through a highly ballistic BLG channel. Our results show that BLG-superconductor hybrids offer a controllable platform where quantum dots and quantum point contacts can be well combined with superconductivity.
articles.summary_en: Researchers integrated bilayer graphene with superconducting NbSe₂ to create gate-defined quantum dots and spectroscopic devices. Measurements detected an induced superconducting gap of up to 80 μeV extending over more than 1 μm, supporting highly ballistic graphene–superconductor hybrid platforms.

articles.title_original: A spiking neural network-in-logic architecture based on reconfigurable molybdenum disulfide dual-gate transistors with ferroelectric gating
articles.title_en: Ferroelectric MoS₂ Transistors Enable Reconfigurable Spiking Neural Networks
articles.excerpt_original: Efficient processing of high-dimensional perceptual data is a challenge in modern electronics, as neuromorphic systems typically process all input features indiscriminately, leading to excessive neuronal activation and high energy consumption. A key issue is the lack of a hardware mechanism to suppress task-irrelevant information at the front-end before neuromorphic computation and preserve reconfigurability. Here we report a spiking neural network-in-logic computing platform in which the front-end logic and spiking neural networks are co-designed to perform task-directed input selection at the hardware level before spike generation, thereby reducing unnecessary neuronal activation. To implement this, we develop reconfigurable field-effect transistors based on dual-gate molybdenum disulfide devices incorporating a ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide layer. These transistors support logic, synaptic and neuronal primitives within a unified device platform. The reconfigurable transistors, which are fabricated using back-end-of-line-compatible processes, are organized into reconfigurable tiles whose roles can be reassigned across tasks, allowing logic-driven input selection to reshape the effective scale of downstream spiking neural networks. The computing architecture is validated using the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology and Street View House Numbers benchmarks, and its system-level energy scaling with task-dependent input complexity is evaluated using real-world multitask inference. Reconfigurable dual-gate ferroelectric transistors that exhibit logic, neuronal and synapse functionalities can provide logic-based spatial pruning of inputs for a spiking neural network, reducing unnecessary neuronal activation and improving energy efficiency.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed back-end-of-line-compatible dual-gate molybdenum disulfide transistors with ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide gating that combine logic, synaptic, and neuronal functions. A reconfigurable hardware architecture used these devices for task-directed input selection, reducing unnecessary neural activation and improving energy efficiency in benchmarked inference tasks.

articles.title_original: Metal Cation Chemistry and Amorphous Structure Governing Hydrogen Tolerance in Oxide Semiconductor Channels for 3D DRAM
articles.title_en: Amorphous ITGO oxide improves hydrogen tolerance for 3D DRAM channels
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT This study analyzed hydrogen tolerance in oxide semiconductors subjected to high‐temperature H 2 annealing (400–600°C), considering different metal species and crystallinities. First, various amorphous ternary oxides with fixed 1:1 at.% cation ratios were evaluated to isolate elemental effects; in the order Zn, Ga, In, and Sn, thickness retention improved while variations in carrier concentration ( n e ) and Hall mobility ( µ Hall ) decreased. Next, ternary oxide films with identical compositions were tuned by pre‐annealing temperature to obtain crystalline or amorphous phase; the crystalline films exhibited enhanced etching and larger changes in n e and µ Hall that are consistent with grain boundary effects. Guided by these observations, amorphous In–Sn–Ga–O (ITGO) was benchmarked against conventional In–Ga–Zn–O (IGZO). The ITGO film maintained a thickness change below 1% with limited Hall variation after H 2 annealing at 600°C. By contrast, the IGZO film exhibited an abrupt increase in n e exceeding three orders of magnitude after H 2 annealing at 500°C, then exhibited etching at 600°C. The application of ITGO in a field‐effect transistor preserved switching characteristics after H 2 annealing up to 600°C, indicating its potential as a channel material for dynamic random‐access memory compatible with high‐temperature hydrogen thermal budgets.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that amorphous In–Sn–Ga–O (ITGO) oxide semiconductor films maintained thickness and electrical stability after hydrogen annealing at up to 600°C, outperforming conventional In–Ga–Zn–O. Field-effect transistor results indicate potential compatibility with high-temperature processing for 3D DRAM.

articles.title_original: Field- and Confinement-Modulated Unconventional Electroosmotic Flow in Two-Dimensional Graphene Nanochannels
articles.title_en: Graphene Nanochannels Enable Field-Controlled Electroosmotic Ion Transport
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Precise control of water and ion transport in nanochannels is fundamental to the development of functional nanofluidic devices. Recent experimental advances have enabled the exploration of nanoscale transport phenomena through the construction of two-dimensional channels with atomically tunable widths. Here, we show that unconventional electroosmotic flow occurring without an electric double layer (EDL) in two-dimensional nanochannels can be modulated by both the applied electric field and the channel width. Significant electroosmotic flow is observed in narrow channels when a single ion permeates under an external field. Free energy calculations of ion permeation events reveal that the flux is induced by channel selectivity for chloride ions over sodium ions. The flux undergoes an unexpected significant decrease when the channel broadens to a width of about 16 Å. This transition is attributed to the reduced permeation events of Bjerrum pairs and to altered free ion mobility by water orientational ordering under an electric field. These results offer new insights into the mechanisms of field-controlled transport in nanoscale channels, informing the design of molecular transport systems and energy-efficient separation technologies.
articles.summary_en: ACS research shows that two-dimensional graphene nanochannels can generate and modulate electroosmotic flow without an electric double layer. The findings clarify ion-selective transport mechanisms relevant to molecular transport systems and energy-efficient separation technologies.

articles.title_original: Wood Engraving Picture-inspired Wearable Flexible Hydrogel Sensors Enabled by Conformal Polyvinyl Alcohol/MXene Composite Ink
articles.title_en: Wood-Engraving-Inspired MXene Hydrogel Enables Patterned Wearable Sensors
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Flexible hydrogel sensors show great utilization potential in the development of wearable devices. Nevertheless, issues such as unsatisfactory sensitivity, intricate fabrication processes, and substantial cost continue to impede their widespread application. Furthermore, a significant challenge resides in developing a convenient method to mold the flexible hydrogel into a variety of shapes, thereby fulfilling the different scenario requirements. Herein, we report a cost-effective, multifunctional polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/multilayer MXene composite PMI hydrogel, which is crosslinked by the addition of sodium tetraborate with the dynamic benzyl boronate ester crosslinking for next-generation wearable sensors. It shows good real-time detection capability in human movement and physiological signal monitoring, as well as speech recognition. However, the plasticity of the aforementioned hydrogel still fails to meet the requirements for the preparation of finely patterned sensors. Inspired by the preparation process of wood engraving pictures, we develop a two-step strategy to fabricate different complex shapes of wearable flexible hydrogel sensors: (1) utilizing thick PVA/MXene precursor ink to create different complex patterns with high resolution; (2) spraying sodium tetraborate solution to fix the patterns quickly. Based on this method, we further explore the application of PMI hydrogel sensors as a flexible wearable device to achieve remote gesture control of the driving paths of car and ship models. Our study strongly demonstrates the promising development potential of PMI hydrogel in the field of flexible wearable human-technology interaction.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a polyvinyl alcohol/multilayer MXene hydrogel ink that can be rapidly fixed into complex, high-resolution sensor patterns. The flexible sensors detected movement, physiological signals, and speech, and enabled remote gesture control of model vehicles.

articles.title_original: Band edge shifts with polarisation switching in a 2D ferroelectric heterostructure
articles.title_en: Polarisation switching shifts band edges in 2D ferroelectric heterostructures
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract There is rising interest in two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectrics, particularly as functional components in 2D heterostructures using their reconfigurable polarisation to create low-power memory devices. Understanding and optimising their application will require investigations that can unravel, at the nanoscale, the effect of ferroelectric switching on the local electronic structure. Using contact mode scanning tunnelling spectroscopy (CM-STS), we observe polarisation-dependent band-edge shifts in an all 2D heterostructure that combines the ferroelectric CuInP_2S_6 (CIPS) with the semiconductor WSe_2 . We employ scanning probe microscopy to characterise the polarisation and conductivity in the CIPS layer, and correlate these measurements with CM-STS spectra, revealing changes from p-type to n-type doping in the WSe_2 layer as the out-of-plane polarisation of the underlying CIPS is switched by the external electric field. The data demonstrate the importance of considering the channel and contact resistances, along with tip-induced-band-bending, when using the tunnelling current to probe the local density of states in 2D semiconductor heterostructures. The significant band-edge shift of 0.8 eV demonstrates efficient coupling of the semiconductor to the polarisation field in the ferroelectric, consistent with clean interfaces in the heterostructure without dead layers. The results show that probing the local density of states by CM-STS gives valuable insight into 2D ferroelectric based electronics and enables direct correlation between electronic structure and functional properties.
articles.summary_en: Researchers observed a 0.8 eV polarisation-dependent band-edge shift in WSe₂ coupled to ferroelectric CuInP₂S₆. The switching changed WSe₂ from p-type to n-type doping, highlighting potential for low-power 2D memory and electronics.

articles.title_original: Up/down-conversion of infrared light by few-layer graphene polytypes
articles.title_en: Few-Layer Graphene Enables Infrared Photon Up- and Down-Conversion
articles.excerpt_original: Optical nonlinearity of materials with broken inversion symmetry enables two-photon processes where an incoming pair of photons can generate an up-converted photon with the combined frequency, or a high-energy photon can be split into a correlated pair of down-converted photons. Here, we identify few-layer graphene films that offer up/down-conversion capability in the infrared spectral range. For mixed stacking tetralayers (ABCB), which are non-centrosymmetric 2D crystals, we find highly efficient nearly resonant up/down-conversion of [$ω_1,ω_2$] photon pairs into/from a photon with $0.7$eV$<Ω=ω_1+ω_2<1.1$eV. We also note that a pronounced second-order nonlinearity in the spectral range of $0.7$eV$<Ω<0.9$eV can be promoted in rhombohedral tri- and tetralayers by asymmetrical encapsulation. Potentially, for fibers coated with few-layer graphene, this opens the door for ``in fiber" production of photon pairs with correlated polarizations.
articles.summary_en: OpenAlex research identifies mixed-stacking few-layer graphene films with efficient infrared up- and down-conversion, particularly in non-centrosymmetric ABCB tetralayers. The findings suggest potential use in fiber-integrated generation of correlated photon pairs, though practical device validation is still needed.

articles.title_original: Auxeticity in Perforated 2D MXene Metamaterials
articles.title_en: Simulations Reveal Tunable Auxeticity in Perforated MXene Metamaterials
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Recent advances in nanoscale fabrication enable atomic-scale manipulation of 2D materials by introducing engineered pores and perforations. This provides new opportunities to tailor functional properties for applications such as selective ion transport, desalination membranes, and molecular filtration. Despite studies on auxeticity in perforated graphene and other 2D materials, the auxetic response of perforated MXene nanostructures remains unexplored. In this work, large-scale reactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations comprising up to 1.3 million atoms are employed to investigate the mechanical response of perforated monolayer titanium-based MXene metamaterials. The simulations use a ReaxFF force field validated against experimental measurements and first-principles calculations of structural and mechanical properties. Architectures containing perforations with straight or sinusoidally curved ligaments are systematically examined under uniaxial tension and compression over a range of geometric parameters and temperatures (1 K to 450 K), from the onset of deformation to fracture. The results demonstrate that MXene metamaterials exhibit a tunable negative Poisson’s ratio over the entire temperature range investigated, approaching -1 for Ti2CO2 and Ti3C2O2 structures featuring rectangular perforations with an aspect ratio of 5 and a ligament thickness to unit cell length ratio of 0.1. Atomistic stress analysis reveals alternating in-plane shear stresses at the junctions that induce rotational deformation of the ligaments. This rotating-junction mechanism is coupled with out-of-plane deflections arising from the low bending rigidity of atomically thin materials, producing complex 3D deformations. The strain range over which auxeticity is maintained is expanded
articles.summary_en: Large-scale molecular-dynamics simulations show that perforated titanium-based MXene monolayers can sustain tunable negative Poisson’s ratios across 1–450 K, approaching −1 in selected architectures. The findings may inform mechanically engineered membranes and molecular-filtration structures, although they remain simulation-based.

articles.title_original: Predictive modelling and experimental analysis of radiation-resistant MXene–silicon heterojunction solar cells
articles.title_en: MXene–Silicon Solar Cells Retain 84% Efficiency Under Radiation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract MXene-silicon heterojunction solar cells (Ti 3 C 2 T x -Si) have become a potential candidate for radiation-tolerant photovoltaic (PV) applications, specifically in harsh space conditions. In this study, a combination of predictive modeling and experimental verification is used to evaluate the degradation characteristics of Ti 3 C 2 T x - Si solar cells under proton and electron irradiation. The study indicates that Ti 3 C 2 T x and Si heterojunction devices can be used to achieve a superior yield, maintaining over 84% of the original power conversion efficiency (PCE), as compared to conventional Si solar cells that can only maintain 55% efficiency under the same exposure. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, and Atom Probe Tomography (APT) reveal the interfacial stability of the MXene layers that alleviates the radiation induced structural damage. A physics-based digital twin (DT) framework is applied to the synthetic degradation data, which achieved a high prediction accuracy of 90% (R 2 > 0.96) using a training model based on Random Forest Regression (RFR), which in turn can aid to forecast the device performance with better accuracy. The PV performance parameters like the open circuit voltage (V OC ), short circuit current density (J SC ), fill factor (FF) and PCE are studied as functions of mission-relevant exposure durations. This hybrid approach of machine learning (ML)-aided modeling, combined with in situ experimental verification develops a solid framework for real-time health monitoring and lifetime prediction of PV devices, making it highly suitable for deployment in radiation-intensive orbital environments. Clinical Trial Registration: Not applicable. This study is not a clinical trial and does not involve any medical intervention or human
articles.summary_en: Researchers combined experiments and predictive modelling to assess Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene–silicon heterojunction solar cells under proton and electron irradiation. The devices reportedly retained more than 84% of their initial efficiency, while a digital-twin model achieved R² above 0.96 for degradation prediction, indicating potential for radiation-tolerant space photovoltaics.

articles.title_original: MXene-based interface-engineering electrocatalysts and artificial intelligence-driven strategies for advanced anion exchange membrane water and seawater electrolysis
articles.title_en: MXene Interface Engineering Advances AEM Water and Seawater Electrolysis
articles.excerpt_original: Green hydrogen production through water electrolysis is a promising pathway for renewable-energy integration and low-carbon development. Among electrolysis technologies, Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis (AEMWE) is attracting increasing attention because it enables alkaline operation, uses earth-abundant catalysts, and can use lower-cost system components. However, translating high electrocatalytic activity from three-electrode testing to membrane electrode assembly (MEA) operation remains challenging due to interfacial resistance, catalyst-ionomer incompatibility, mass-transport limitations, membrane degradation, and long-term durability issues. In this context, two-dimensional MXene-based materials have emerged as promising platforms for AEM water and seawater electrolysis owing to their high electrical conductivity, tunable surface terminations, hydrophilicity, structural flexibility, and strong interfacial coupling with catalytic phases. This review critically discusses recent progress in MXene-based catalysts and membrane-related systems, focusing on heterostructure engineering, multicomponent nanocomposites, defect modulation, and surface/interface regulation. The roles of MXenes as conductive scaffolds, charge-transfer mediators, adsorption-energy regulators, catalyst-dispersion supports, and mass-transport promoters are examined in relation to the kinetics and stability of HER/OER. Special attention is given to seawater electrolysis, where chloride-induced corrosion, competing chlorine evolution, salt precipitation, and catalyst/membrane instability remain major barriers. Recent advances in MXene-containing anion-exchange membranes are also discussed in terms of structure-property relationships involving surface terminations, polymer-MXene compatibility
articles.summary_en: This review examines MXene-based catalysts, heterostructures, and anion-exchange membranes for improving interfacial charge transfer, catalytic kinetics, mass transport, and durability in alkaline and seawater electrolysis. It identifies chloride corrosion, competing chlorine evolution, salt precipitation, and membrane instability as key barriers to commercialization.

articles.title_original: Energy‐Responsive Nb 2 C MXene‐Based Superwetting Sponge With Coupled Photothermal‐Electrothermal Heating for Multifunctional Environmental Remediation
articles.title_en: MXene-Based Sponge Combines Photothermal Heating with Oil–Water Separation
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Energy‐responsive porous materials capable of on‐demand thermal regulation are highly desirable for controlling interfacial transport in complex environmental systems. Herein, an energy‐responsive superwetting sponge is developed by integrating Nb 2 C MXene with CuO nanostructures and polyaniline within a hierarchical porous framework, followed by low‐surface‐energy modification. The composite exhibits broadband light absorption and electrical conductivity, enabling efficient photothermal and electrothermal conversion. Under solar irradiation and low‐voltage stimulation, rapid and uniform temperature elevation is achieved, and the combined photothermal‐electrothermal mode demonstrates enhanced heating performance compared to individual modes. Meanwhile, the superhydrophobic porous structure and active thermal regulation synergistically delay ice nucleation and growth. As a multifunctional platform, the material also enables effective separation of complex oily emulsions and removal of organic contaminants with excellent recyclability. This work provides a versatile MXene‐based strategy for energy‐adaptive porous materials toward advanced environmental remediation and interfacial transport control.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a Nb₂C MXene, CuO, and polyaniline porous sponge that provides coupled photothermal and electrothermal heating under sunlight or low voltage. Its superhydrophobic structure delays ice formation and supports recyclable separation of oily emulsions and removal of organic contaminants.

articles.title_original: Interface-engineered SrFeO3-MXene hybrids as highly efficient bifunctional electrocatalysts for overall water splitting
articles.title_en: Interface-engineered SrFeO3–MXene hybrids improve water-splitting catalysis
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed SrFeO3–MXene hybrid electrocatalysts designed to efficiently catalyze both reactions required for overall water splitting. The work highlights interface engineering as a route to improved bifunctional catalytic performance, with potential relevance to hydrogen production.

articles.title_original: Thermally conductive polybenzimidazole/boron nitride composite film via an organic solvent-free sol-gel process
articles.title_en: Solvent-Free Process Produces Thermally Conductive PBI–Boron Nitride Films
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a polybenzimidazole/boron nitride composite film using an organic solvent-free sol-gel process. The work targets thermally conductive polymer films for thermal-management applications while reducing solvent use during processing.

articles.title_original: Polymorphic crystallites model for monolayer amorphous materials
articles.title_en: Polymorphic crystallites identified in monolayer amorphous materials
articles.excerpt_original: Establishing atomistic models of amorphous materials remains a central challenge in materials science. Here, we examine three representative multicomponent monolayer systems using first-principles-trained machine-learning potentials and an energy-guided Monte Carlo structural-search workflow. For monolayer amorphous boron nitride (maBN), independent density-functional-theory single-point calculations confirm that the ensemble generated by the machine-learning potential (MLP)-driven search is lower in energy on average than an extended-Tersoff-generated ensemble. Across the sampled maBN structures, local-ring classification combined with strict connected-domain analysis identifies h-BN-like, o-B2N2-like, and o-B4N4-like crystallite domains together with mixed medium-range order. Only individual samples containing at least two distinct phase-pure crystallite-domain types are classified as polymorphic crystallites. The same analysis finds coexisting hexagonal and tetragonal domains in monolayer amorphous LiCl and graphene-like, h-BN-like, borophene-like, and mixed-order regions in monolayer amorphous BCN. Five-nanosecond MLP molecular-dynamics trajectories at 300 K show that the candidate structures are dynamically persistent on the simulated timescale. These results support a polymorphic-crystallite description for the selected model systems, while experimental discrimination from alternative continuous-random-network descriptions will require medium-range-order-sensitive measurements.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used machine-learning potentials and Monte Carlo structural searches to model amorphous monolayer boron nitride, lithium chloride and BCN. The analysis identified persistent graphene-like, h-BN-like, borophene-like and other crystallite domains, while noting that experimental validation is still needed.

articles.title_original: Chiral Antiferromagnetism from Momentum-Space Resonance in a 2D Semiconductor
articles.title_en: 2D GdGaI Semiconductor Exhibits Chiral Antiferromagnetism and Anomalous Hall Effect
articles.excerpt_original: Understanding the principles governing the emergence of chiral quantum phases is a fundamental challenge, not only for uncovering new mechanisms of quantum-state formation but also for realizing giant electronic responses and transport phenomena arising from chirality and topology. While Fermi-surface instabilities in metals can stabilize complex ordered states through multiple competing scattering channels, their microscopic origin is often obscured by the complexity of the underlying electronic structure, limiting the development of general microscopic design principles. Here, we introduce a complementary strategy based on the simplicity of semiconductor band extrema. Using the layered van der Waals semiconductor GdGaI, whose low-energy electronic structure consists of simple electron and hole valleys, we discover the spontaneous emergence of an intertwined chiral triple-$q$ antiferromagnetic state accompanied by a cooperative reconstruction of the electron-hole band edges, beyond the conventional expectation of a single-$q$ ground state. This collective reconstruction generates substantial momentum-space Berry curvature, giving rise to a pronounced spontaneous anomalous Hall effect despite the semiconducting character and negligible net magnetization. Remarkably, this chiral state is realized within an atomically well-defined ($\approx2a$), topologically nontrivial magnetic texture, showing that such collective quantum states can emerge at an exceptionally small length scale from a simple two-dimensional magnetic semiconductor. More broadly, our results introduce a remarkably simple design concept for chiral quantum matter: using simple semiconductor band extrema as building blocks for resonance-like interplay in momentum space, providing a route to Berry curvature,
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a chiral triple-q antiferromagnetic state in layered van der Waals semiconductor GdGaI, driven by momentum-space resonance between simple electron and hole valleys. The atomically small magnetic texture produces substantial Berry curvature and a pronounced spontaneous anomalous Hall effect despite negligible net magnetization, suggesting a design route for chiral quantum materials.

articles.title_original: Self‐Limiting Oxide Dielectric Enables Interface‐State Engineering in p ‐Type m‐GaTe Transistors Toward Bio‐Inspired Visual Recognition
articles.title_en: Self-Limiting Oxide Dielectric Enables Neuromorphic GaTe Transistors
articles.excerpt_original: The development of efficient artificial intelligence hardware has spurred interest in neuromorphic systems that unify sensing, memory, and computing. Optoelectronic synaptic transistors are appealing due to their rapid response times, broad spectral range, and low energy consumption. However, most 2D material-based systems require complex structural and interfacial engineering, which limits scalability and stability. Moreover, the lack of air-stable p-type 2D semiconductors hinders the creation of energy-efficient architectures. In this study, we present monoclinic GaTe (m-GaTe), an intrinsically p-type layered semiconductor, as a robust alternative. Through chemical vapor deposition, we achieve orientation-controlled epitaxial growth of high-quality m-GaTe, and reveal a unique self-limiting surface oxidation. This native oxide serves as both an encapsulation layer and a dielectric, introducing interfacial charge-trapping states that facilitate effective modulation of hole transport in p-type m-GaTe transistors. By exploiting these oxide-mediated properties and engineered contacts, we achieve tunable memristive switching and synaptic plasticity in a single p-type transistor. More importantly, the strong ultraviolet photoresponse of m-GaTe supports a device-array-based sensing system that, when paired with convolutional neural networks, excels in ultraviolet feature extraction and bio-inspired visual perception. This work offers a scalable and reliable pathway to integrated opto-neuromorphic systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed air-stable, p-type monoclinic GaTe transistors with a native oxide that functions as both encapsulation and dielectric. The devices demonstrate tunable memristive switching, synaptic plasticity, and ultraviolet feature extraction for bio-inspired visual recognition.

articles.title_original: Enhanced emission from boron-vacancy center in rhombohedral boron nitride
articles.title_en: Rhombohedral boron nitride boosts boron-vacancy emission
articles.excerpt_original: Boron nitride is a layered crystal whose properties depend on how its atomic sheets are stacked. Its negatively charged boron vacancy is a well-established magnetic defect that can be prepared and read out optically, but in the common hexagonal form it emits very little light, because the symmetry of the surrounding lattice forbids the relevant optical transition. Here we show, using first-principles calculations, that stacking the sheets in the rhombohedral sequence instead removes this restriction and increases the emitted intensity by one to two orders of magnitude, while the magnetic properties remain comparable or improve. We predict that the resulting emission is bright enough for a single defect to be addressed at room temperature, and that a sharp emission line, absent in the hexagonal form, should appear on cooling. Stacking order therefore acts as a design parameter for tailoring the quantum properties of defects embedded in layered materials.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations show that rhombohedral stacking increases boron-vacancy emission intensity by one to two orders of magnitude while preserving or improving magnetic properties. The predicted room-temperature single-defect emission could support quantum sensing and other quantum-device applications.

articles.title_original: Optical nonlinearity induced UV luminescence in sp2-bonded boron nitride films
articles.title_en: Rhombohedral Boron Nitride Films Enable Efficient UV-C Luminescence
articles.excerpt_original: Polytypism, arising from the different arrangements of successive two-dimensional (2D) atomic planes, strongly influences various physical properties of sp²-bonded layered boron nitrides (BN), including optical nonlinearity and high-frequency light generation through up-conversion of longer wavelengths, by altering the crystal symmetry. Rhombohedral BN (rBN), one such polytype, stacks its 2D atomic sheets in an ABC sequence and, unlike AA'-stacked hexagonal BN (hBN), lacks inversion symmetry. This centrosymmetry breaking enables second-harmonic generation (SHG), which extends into the UV-C spectral region due to its wide bandgap. Here, we demonstrate that this UV-C SHG can be generated in metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown rBN films and effectively used to stimulate various defect-related photoluminescence (PL). We focus on the PL of the C300 color center (CBCN defect) at 4.1 eV, notable for its bright emission and single-photon purity. By qualitatively comparing the spectral features of this luminescence in rBN with those recorded for centrosymmetric reference hBN specimens that cannot demonstrate SHG but can exhibit two-photon absorption (TPA), we highlight the distinct roles of SHG in rBN and two-photon absorption in hBN in generating the 4.1 eV PL, and further emphasize the superior efficiency of SHG as a pathway for inducing the defect emission, using far longer-wavelength photons.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated UV-C second-harmonic generation in MOVPE-grown rhombohedral boron nitride films, exploiting broken inversion symmetry. The process efficiently stimulated 4.1 eV defect-related photoluminescence, highlighting potential for nonlinear photonics and single-photon emission.

articles.title_original: Scalable Synthesis of Er-Yb Co-doped Monolayer WS2 on Sapphire via Halide-Assisted CVD for Advanced Optoelectronics
articles.title_en: Scalable CVD synthesis of Er–Yb-doped monolayer WS₂ for optoelectronics
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a halide-assisted CVD method for producing Er–Yb co-doped monolayer WS₂ on sapphire. The scalable approach targets advanced optoelectronic applications.

articles.title_original: Ultra−Sensitive 2D Dion−Jacobson Perovskite Phototransistors for Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
articles.title_en: 2D Perovskite Phototransistors Enable Ultra-Sensitive Neuromorphic Vision
articles.excerpt_original: Metal halide perovskite (MHP) semiconductors demonstrate significant advantages over traditional semiconductor materials in next-generation weak-light-responsive devices, owing to their exceptional photoelectric conversion capabilities and outstanding charge transport properties. Under illumination with a power density as low as 0.1 µW/cm2, these devices can efficiently respond to faint optical signals, achieving an ultrahigh detectivity of 1017 Jones-highlighting their exceptional sensitivity in low weak−light conditions. Furthermore, driven by intrinsic charge trap/de−trap dynamics, the devices successfully emulate fundamental biological synaptic behaviors, including optical pulse−modulated transitions from short−term to long−term memory. Leveraging these tunable synaptic characteristics, we further demonstrate complex visual learning simulations. Specifically, the system successfully modeled a facial recognition training process, where increasing optical stimulation progressively enhanced facial feature extraction, closely mimicking human visual cognition. By exploiting the adjustable conductance of the improved synaptic device, we construct convolutional neural networks to execute synaptic weight modifications. After 100 training epochs, the proposed system achieves a remarkable recognition accuracy of 98.91% on handwritten digit classification tasks. Collectively, these results systematically underscore the immense potential of BDASnI4 FETs as highly stable, multifunctional hardware platforms for next−generation photoelectrically integrated artificial visual systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report Dion–Jacobson perovskite phototransistors that detect optical signals as weak as 0.1 µW/cm², with reported detectivity of 10¹⁷ Jones. The devices emulate synaptic memory and achieved 98.91% handwritten-digit recognition in a simulated visual-learning system.

articles.title_original: High-performance graphene/aluminum composites: progress and challenges from an industrial perspective
articles.title_en: Review Examines Industrialization of Graphene–Aluminum Composites
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene/aluminum (Gr/Al) composites are regarded as a promising class of lightweight, high-performance materials for aerospace, automotive, and electronics applications. Graphene’s exceptional mechanical, thermal, and electrical properties are integrated with aluminum’s favorable density and formability. From an industrial perspective, different methods for producing graphene are analyzed, and graphene/aluminum composites are discussed. The industrialization bottlenecks and path strategies for high-performance Gr/Al composites are analyzed. The major bottlenecks are uniform dispersion of graphene in Al matrix, suppression of the harmful Al 4 C 3 interfacial phase, and cost control for large-scale production. The former two problems are addressed by the development of low-cost graphene surface modification technology. The latter problem can be solved by combining different composite technologies, such as spark plasma sintering and casting, which enables excellent microstructure controllability and efficiency. This dual-path framework is provided as a practical reference for the commercialization of Gr/Al composites.
articles.summary_en: An academic review assesses graphene–aluminum composites for aerospace, automotive, and electronics applications, highlighting dispersion, interfacial Al₄C₃ formation, and production cost as key scale-up barriers. It proposes surface modification and combined sintering/casting approaches to support commercialization.

articles.title_original: Graphene‐Analogous Monolayer Boron Pnictides for High‐Mobility Electronics
articles.title_en: Confined Growth Produces High-Mobility Monolayer Boron Pnictides
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Monolayer hexagonal phase boron pnictides are graphene‐analogous semiconductors, which are predicted to inherit a Dirac‐like electronic structure that promises intrinsically high carrier mobility for next‐generation electronics. However, their development has been experimentally hindered by the inherent instability of the hexagonal phase under ambient and growth conditions. Here, we overcome this fundamental challenge by employing a sub‐nanometer‐scale confined growth strategy within single‐walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), which enables the first synthesis of stable, monolayer hexagonal boron phosphide (h‐BP) and boron arsenide (h‐BAs). The interfacial interactions between host‐guest materials within the confined space are shown to be crucial for obtaining intrinsically metastable hexagonal phase boron pnictides (B‐Pn) which are inaccessible through conventional synthesis methods. Notably, the h‐BP‐filled s‐SWCNTs heterostructure (h‐BP@s‐SWCNTs) exhibits a near 15‐fold enhancement in carrier mobility compared to pristine s‐SWCNTs (the highest reaching up to 526.9 cm 2 ·V −1 ·s −1 ), which represents a high‐performance level for FETs based on aligned s‐SWCNTs arrays. This research marks a breakthrough for interface engineering and band structure modulation to access metastable low‐dimensional nanostructures, toward next‐generation interface‐engineered, high‐performance nanoelectronics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized stable monolayer hexagonal boron phosphide and boron arsenide inside single-walled carbon nanotubes, overcoming the instability of these graphene-analogous semiconductors. The boron phosphide–nanotube heterostructure achieved carrier mobility up to 526.9 cm²·V⁻¹·s⁻¹, nearly 15 times that of pristine semiconducting nanotubes, highlighting potential for high-performance nanoelectronics.

articles.title_original: Facilitating the activation of wide bandgap hexagonal boron nitride via 222 nm far UV-C for efficient photocatalytic degradation of recalcitrant PFAS
articles.title_en: 222 nm UV-C Activates hBN for PFAS Degradation
articles.summary_en: Researchers report using 222 nm far-UVC to activate wide-bandgap hexagonal boron nitride for photocatalytic degradation of persistent PFAS. The work indicates a potential water-treatment route for recalcitrant contaminants, subject to validation of degradation efficiency and byproducts.

articles.title_original: Two-Dimensional Materials toward CMOS-Compatible Scalable Quantum Hardware
articles.title_en: Two-Dimensional Materials for CMOS-Compatible Scalable Quantum Hardware
articles.excerpt_original: Manufacturability is one of several constraints on developing solid-state quantum processors, along with qubit performance, control, connectivity, cryogenic operation, and fault tolerance. Chemical residues, structural disorder, and non-uniform interfaces introduced during fabrication can compromise qubit coherence. Two-dimensional (2D) materials, with their atomically thin crystals and van der Waals interfaces, offer routes to address some of these challenges. Their concurrent development as next-generation CMOS channel materials motivates an examination of whether relevant processes can be transferred to quantum chips. This Perspective evaluates the opportunities and limitations of 2D materials for CMOS-compatible quantum hardware.
articles.summary_en: A perspective examines how atomically thin 2D materials and van der Waals interfaces could address fabrication challenges in solid-state quantum processors, including disorder, residues, and interface non-uniformity. It evaluates whether CMOS-compatible processes can transfer to quantum-chip manufacturing while considering qubit performance, connectivity, cryogenics, and fault tolerance.

articles.title_original: Tailoring complex coupling for efficient synchronization of semiconductor lasers
articles.title_en: Tailoring Coupling Enables Efficient Synchronization of Semiconductor Lasers
articles.excerpt_original: A grand challenge for laser synchronization is the intrinsic frequency disorder. We build an experimental platform for programming the complex coupling coefficients of semiconductor lasers to promote frequency and phase locking. The coupling amplitude between every pair of lasers in an array is tuned to scale with their frequency difference. Coupling phases are scanned to meet the phase matching conditions for constructive interference of coupled fields. The minimum coupling budget for global synchronization is significantly reduced, as shown experimentally for three vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers with intrinsic frequency detuning. The customized coupling offers an efficient approach to stable synchronization of semiconductor laser arrays for coherent beam combining.
articles.summary_en: Researchers experimentally demonstrate programmable coupling between semiconductor lasers to achieve frequency and phase locking despite intrinsic frequency differences. The approach reduces the coupling required for global synchronization and could support coherent beam combining in laser arrays.

articles.title_original: Interface-Induced performance in GO/MXene nanocomposite membrane for dye filtration
articles.title_en: Interface-Engineered GO/MXene Membrane for Dye Filtration
articles.summary_en: Academic research examines how interfaces influence the performance of a graphene oxide/MXene nanocomposite membrane for dye filtration. The study is relevant to membrane-based water treatment, but the available record provides no performance data or commercial involvement.

articles.title_original: Orientation-dependent frictional anisotropy in Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene/SiC heterojunctions
articles.title_en: Orientation-Dependent Friction in MXene–SiC Heterojunctions
articles.summary_en: Academic research examines how orientation affects frictional anisotropy in Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene/SiC heterojunctions. The findings may inform the design of low-friction interfaces and protective materials, although no commercial application is reported.

articles.title_original: Valley-dependent electron optics using quantum dots in bilayer graphene
articles.title_en: Valley-Dependent Electron Optics Demonstrated with Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
articles.summary_en: APS reports research on controlling valley-dependent electron optics using quantum dots in bilayer graphene. The work is relevant to graphene-based quantum and semiconductor device architectures, although no application or commercialization details are provided.

articles.title_original: Tailoring the performance of ball-milled silicon-glucose-graphene anodes: The critical role of graphene type and structure
articles.title_en: Study identifies graphene structure as key to silicon–glucose anode performance
articles.summary_en: Academic research examines how graphene type and structure affect ball-milled silicon–glucose–graphene anodes. The findings may inform graphene selection and electrode design for improved energy-storage performance.

articles.title_original: Nonradiative energy transfer between boron vacancies in hexagonal boron nitride and other two-dimensional materials
articles.title_en: Nonradiative Energy Transfer from Boron Vacancies in hBN to 2D Materials
articles.summary_en: Academic research examines nonradiative energy transfer between boron vacancies in hexagonal boron nitride and other two-dimensional materials. The work may inform nanoscale optoelectronic and quantum-device design, but no specific application or commercialization is identified.

articles.title_original: Diagnostic Dual Frugal for Pulsed Magnetized Confinement Platforms: Villari/hBN Sensing, Low-Cost Brillouin/Raman Backscatter and Inter-Shot Machine Learning
articles.title_en: Low-Cost Dual Diagnostics for Pulsed Magnetized Fusion Platforms
articles.excerpt_original: Description This work proposes a frugal dual diagnostic architecture for pulsed magnetized confinement and magnetized target fusion platforms, designed for independent laboratories, educational facilities and low-budget experimental environments. The concept combines two complementary diagnostic channels: A Villari/hBN sensor, previously proposed for simultaneous magnetic-field and mechanical-stress monitoring through VB spin centers in hexagonal boron nitride. A low-cost Brillouin/Raman stimulated backscatter channel, using an optical pick-off, dichroic or interference filters and fast photodiodes to provide coarse discrimination between SBS and SRS signals. An optional second-hand Fabry-Pérot etalon is considered for degraded estimation of SBS spectral shifts and therefore approximate plasma-flow and ion-temperature information. The estimated cost of the new optical diagnostic channel is approximately €750–2,000, or up to approximately €2,500 including a second-hand Fabry-Pérot etalon, excluding the hBN sensor and acquisition hardware already considered in the previous work. The architecture deliberately does not attempt to reproduce the performance of dedicated FABS/SABS stations at major laser facilities. Instead, it asks a more modest question: How much scientifically useful diagnostic information can be recovered with a deliberately degraded but coherent and testable system? The proposed system aims to retain: time-resolved SBS/SRS reflectivity; coarse SBS/SRS spectral discrimination; correlation between optical and Villari/hBN signals; shot-to-shot anomaly detection; progressive extraction of diagnostic features; and, optionally, degraded estimates of plasma flow and ion temperature. articles.title_original: rGO/MXene hybrid exhibit fast oxygen reduction reaction catalytic activity
articles.title_en: rGO/MXene Hybrids Enable Fast Oxygen-Reduction Catalysis
articles.excerpt_original: To develop efficient bifunctional electrocatalysts essential for clean energy production, oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) and oxygen evolution reactions (OER) play a crucial role. MXenes, owing to their excellent metallic conductivity, large specific surface area, hydrophilicity, and superior electrochemical properties, are promising materials for electrocatalysis. This chapter highlights the key design principles of MXene-based electrocatalysts, including: Coupling MXene with heteroatomic doping or reduced graphene oxide (rGO) to create highly active synergistic catalytic sites; Constructing 2D/3D MXene assemblies or introducing interlayer spacers to enhance the active surface area and form rapid mass and charge transfer channels; and Protecting the MXene edges or in situ transforming the surface into an energetically active material to prevent oxidation and improve stability. As a result, MXene-based materials perform exceptionally well in various electrocatalytic reactions. Finally, a brief overview of the main challenges and exciting opportunities for the real-world application of rGO/MXene hybrid electrocatalysts is provided.
articles.summary_en: A review chapter outlines design strategies for reduced graphene oxide/MXene electrocatalysts targeting oxygen reduction and evolution reactions. It highlights heteroatom doping, 2D/3D assembly, interlayer spacing, and surface protection as routes to improve activity, mass and charge transfer, and stability.

articles.title_original: Main-group-element-based surface functionalization of MXenes toward advanced tribological applications
articles.title_en: Main-Group Functionalization Advances MXene Tribological Performance
articles.excerpt_original: MXenes are one of the most versatile families of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides due to their metallic conductivity, tunable surface chemistry and excellent mechanical properties. Nevertheless, the practical application of MXenes in lubrication, coatings, energy storage and sensing technologies are still limited by surface oxidation, restacking and poor environmental stability. Thus, surface functionalization has become a key strategy for tailoring the interfacial properties of MXenes. Among the various approaches investigated, main-group chemistry provides unique opportunities for rational surface modification via the formation of strong covalent and coordination interactions involving silicon, phosphorus, sulfur, nitrogen and halogen-containing functionalities. These modifications regulate surface energy, interlayer spacing, and oxidation resistance while simultaneously enhancing tribological performance through tribofilm formation and interlayer shear modulation. This review critically summarizes recent advances in main-group chemistry-driven functionalization and doping of MXenes, highlighting structure–property relationships, mechanistic insights, and future opportunities for the development of durable and high-performance MXene-based tribological systems. Besides cataloguing individual functionalization chemistries, this review critically compares silane-, phosphonic acid-, fluorine-, polymer-, intercalation-, and heteroatom doping-based strategies with one another in terms of achievable friction reduction, environmental (humidity/oxidation) tolerance, and mechanistic maturity. articles.summary_en: A review examines silicon-, phosphorus-, sulfur-, nitrogen- and halogen-based surface functionalization of MXenes to improve oxidation resistance, interlayer shear and friction performance.
